name: Chicken Shawarma with Lemon Yogurt Sauce
why: Middle Eastern street food at home — deeply spiced chicken thighs marinated in coriander, cumin, and cardamom, then pan-seared until charred and served in warm flatbreads with a cooling lemon yogurt sauce. Bold, fragrant, and completely different from anything recently recommended.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1 kg / 2 lb chicken thigh fillets, skinless and boneless
1 tsp ground cayenne pepper (reduce to 1/2 tsp for milder)
Salt and pepper to taste (for sauce)

steps: In a large ziplock bag, combine minced garlic, ground coriander, ground cumin, ground cardamom, cayenne pepper, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, and olive oil. Mix well.
Add the chicken thigh fillets to the bag. Seal tightly, removing excess air, then massage from the outside with your hands to coat every piece evenly.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours (ideally 24 hours for maximum flavour). The chicken can be frozen in the marinade and defrosted before cooking.
In a small bowl, combine Greek yogurt, crushed garlic, ground cumin, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes to let the flavours meld. Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and swirl to coat.
Remove chicken from the marinade (discard excess marinade in the bag). Place chicken thighs in the hot skillet.
Cook undisturbed for 4-5 minutes until nicely charred and golden on the first side.
Flip and cook the other side for 3-4 minutes until cooked through — the chicken should be golden with a spicy crust and reach an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F.
Transfer chicken to a plate and cover loosely with foil. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Slice the rested chicken into strips or bite-sized pieces.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side, or wrap in foil and warm in the oven at 180°C for 5 minutes.
To make a wrap: smear flatbread with yogurt sauce, top with lettuce, tomato slices, red onion, and chicken. Roll up and enjoy.
Alternatively, serve as a shawarma platter: pile sliced chicken alongside flatbreads, lettuce, tomato, red onion, yogurt sauce, and hummus.

pro_tips: The marination time makes or breaks this dish — 24 hours in the fridge gives the cardamom and cumin time to penetrate deeply. If you're short on time, 3 hours still works well, but overnight is transformative.
Don't crowd the pan when cooking — if your skillet is small, cook in two batches. Overcrowding steams the chicken instead of searing it, and you lose that essential charred crust.
